title: Find Users with High Token Usage
summary:
Table: prompts
Columns: user_id int, prompt varchar, tokens int. Unique key: (user_id, prompt). Each row represents a prompt submitted by a user to an AI system along with the number of tokens consumed.
Task: Aggregate each user's prompt count and token usage, then retain users meeting the stipulated high-usage thresholds.
- For each user, calculate the total number of prompts they have submitted.
- For each user, calculate the average tokens used per prompt (Rounded to 2 decimal places).
- Only include users who have submitted at least 3 prompts.
- Only include users who have submitted at least one prompt with tokens greater than their own average token usage.
Ordering: average tokens in descending order, and then by user_id in ascending order.
Example output columns: user_id, prompt_count, avg_tokens.
Source: https://leetcode.doocs.org/en/lc/3793/
Language evidence: official SQL Schema and Pandas Schema templates checked on 2026-11-17.

title: Find Emotionally Consistent Users
summary:
Table: reactions
Columns: user_id int, content_id int, reaction varchar. Unique key: (user_id, content_id). Each row represents a reaction given by a user to a piece of content.
Task: Aggregate reactions for each user and select users meeting the emotion-consistency and minimum-activity requirements below.
- For each user, count the total number of reactions they have given.
- Only include users who have reacted to at least 5 different content items.
- A user is considered emotionally consistent if at least 60% of their reactions are of the same type.
Ordering: reaction_ratio in descending order and then by user_id in ascending order.
Note:
- reaction_ratio should be rounded to 2 decimal places
Example output columns: user_id, dominant_reaction, reaction_ratio.
Source: https://leetcode.doocs.org/en/lc/3808/
Language evidence: official SQL Schema and Pandas Schema templates checked on 2026-11-17.

title: Find Users with Persistent Behavior Patterns
summary:
Table: activity
Columns: user_id int, action_date date, action varchar. Unique key: (user_id, action_date, action). Each row represents a user performing a specific action on a given date.
Task: Find each user's longest run of at least five consecutive days containing exactly one identical action per day. Break equal lengths by action ascending, then start date descending.
- A user is considered behaviorally stable if there exists a sequence of at least 5 consecutive days such that:
- The user performed exactly one action per day during that period.
- The action is the same on all those consecutive days.
- If a user has multiple qualifying sequences, only consider the sequence with the maximum length.
- If multiple qualifying sequences have the same maximum length, consider the sequence with the lexicographically smallest action. If there is still a tie, consider the sequence with the latest start date.
Ordering: streak_length in descending order, then by user_id in ascending order.
Example output columns: user_id, action, streak_length, start_date, end_date.
Source: https://leetcode.doocs.org/en/lc/3832/
Language evidence: official SQL Schema and Pandas Schema templates checked on 2026-11-17.
